name: Post-compromise IAM/account enumeration (situational awareness)
primitive: Overly-broad iam:List*/iam:Get*/*:Describe* on obtained credentials enables full account inventory (cloudfox/pacu/enumerate-iam)
achieved_effect: Full inventory of principals, policies, and reachable services mapped; over-permissioned paths identified
notes: Pwned Labs 'Get Situational Awareness in AWS with Cloudfox', 'Intro to AWS IAM Enumeration'; GetAccountAuthorizationDetails

name: CloudTrail coverage gap (disabled / single-region / no validation)
primitive: No multi-region trail, log-file validation off, not encrypted, or management events not captured
notes: Static blind spot; CIS-benchmark checks; region gaps enable unmonitored activity (ATT&CK T1535)

name: IMDSv1 enabled (HttpTokens optional) on EC2
primitive: Instance metadata options allow IMDSv1 (HttpTokens=optional), making 169.254.169.254 reachable without a session token
notes: Static precursor to SSRF/RCE credential theft; remediate with HttpTokens=required + hop limit 1

name: Loot data from a publicly-shared EBS snapshot
primitive: EBS snapshot with public CreateVolumePermission; attacker in any account creates a volume from it and mounts it
achieved_effect: Filesystem data (secrets, keys, source) recovered from a public EBS snapshot mounted in the attacker's account
notes: Pwned Labs 'Loot Public EBS Snapshots'; also achievable via ec2:ModifySnapshotAttribute to self-share a victim snapshot

name: Lambda environment-variable secret disclosure
primitive: lambda:GetFunction/GetFunctionConfiguration returns plaintext environment variables containing secrets
achieved_effect: Secrets recovered from a Lambda function's environment variables
notes: Posture precursor = unencrypted secrets in env; readable with only function-config read perms

name: Access a publicly-reachable RDS instance
primitive: RDS instance PubliclyAccessible=true with a permissive security group + weak/known/leaked DB creds
achieved_effect: Direct DB connection established to a public RDS endpoint and data read
notes: Pwned Labs 'Pillage Exposed RDS Instances'; posture precursor = public + open SG

name: Restore and loot a publicly-shared RDS snapshot
primitive: RDS/Aurora snapshot shared public (or to attacker account); restored as a new instance in the attacker account
achieved_effect: Database contents read from an instance restored from a public RDS snapshot
notes: Pwned Labs 'Plunder Public RDS Snapshots'

name: S3 replication / Batch Operations data exfiltration
primitive: s3:PutReplicationConfiguration or s3:CreateJob (+iam:PassRole to a replication role) redirects/copies objects to an attacker bucket
achieved_effect: Bucket objects replicated/copied to an attacker-controlled bucket
notes: Pwned Labs 'Abuse S3 Replication and Batch Ops to Exfiltrate Data'

name: Secret recovery from prior S3 object versions
primitive: Bucket versioning enabled + s3:GetObjectVersion/ListObjectVersions; a secret 'removed' in the current object survives in an old version
achieved_effect: Live secret retrieved from a previous object version via GetObjectVersion
notes: Pwned Labs 'Access Secrets with S3 Bucket Versioning'

name: Secrets Manager mass secret exfiltration
primitive: Over-broad secretsmanager:GetSecretValue/ListSecrets (+kms:Decrypt) on obtained credentials
achieved_effect: Plaintext secrets retrieved from Secrets Manager and used for further access
notes: Pwned Labs 'Leverage Leaked Credentials for Pwnage', 'Understand Authentication Mechanisms Using Boto3'

name: SNS abuse for data exfiltration
primitive: sns:Subscribe an attacker endpoint to a topic, or sns:Publish, over an over-permissive topic policy
achieved_effect: Sensitive messages exfiltrated by subscribing an attacker-controlled endpoint to (or publishing on) an SNS topic
notes: Pwned Labs 'Exfiltrate Secrets via Amazon SNS Abuse'

name: SSM Parameter Store SecureString exfiltration
primitive: ssm:GetParameter(s)/GetParametersByPath with WithDecryption on SecureString parameters holding credentials
achieved_effect: Decrypted SecureString parameters (credentials/tokens) exfiltrated
notes: Common secret store alongside Secrets Manager

name: KMS-backed ransomware / data denial
primitive: kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion / kms:DisableKey / re-encrypt with an attacker-imported CMK removes the org's ability to decrypt its data
achieved_effect: Encrypted data (S3/EBS/RDS) rendered inaccessible by disabling/scheduling deletion of the protecting KMS key
notes: Pwned Labs 'Investigate a Ransomware Attack in AWS' (KMS+IAM)

name: API Gateway authorization/restriction bypass
primitive: Missing/misconfigured authorizer, permissive resource policy, or stage/route reachable without the intended IAM/Cognito auth
achieved_effect: A protected API Gateway route reached / its authorization control bypassed
notes: Pwned Labs 'Bypass Restrictions in API Gateway'

name: CI/build-server compromise pivoting to AWS credentials
primitive: Exposed/misconfigured Jenkins/TeamCity/Splunk on EC2 with stored AWS creds or an instance role reachable from the app
achieved_effect: AWS credentials extracted from a compromised CI/admin server and used against the account
notes: Pwned Labs 'Exploit Jenkins in the Cloud', 'Pwn TeamCity in the Cloud', 'Compromise Splunk for AWS Privilege Escalation'

name: Cognito unauthenticated identity pool AWS credential issuance
primitive: Cognito Identity Pool allows unauthenticated identities and its guest IAM role has over-broad permissions
achieved_effect: AWS credentials for the identity-pool unauth role obtained via cognito-identity:GetId + GetCredentialsForIdentity
notes: Pwned Labs 'Abuse Cognito User and Identity Pools'; also user-pool self-signup/writable-attribute abuse

name: Long-lived AWS keys leaked in source repos / container images
primitive: AKIA/ASIA credentials committed to git history, CodeCommit, or baked into Docker image layers
achieved_effect: Valid AWS access keys recovered and authenticated (sts:GetCallerIdentity succeeds)
notes: Pwned Labs 'Hunt for Secrets in Git Repos', 'Uncover Secrets in CodeCommit and Docker'

name: Over-permissive OIDC federation role (CI to AWS)
primitive: IAM OIDC role trust condition on sub/aud is too loose (e.g. wildcards any repo/branch), letting an untrusted CI workload assume the role
achieved_effect: AWS role assumed via an OIDC web-identity token from an attacker-controlled/other CI project (GitLab/GitHub Actions)
notes: Pwned Labs 'Abuse OpenID Connect and GitLab for AWS Access'; check StringLike vs StringEquals on token:sub

name: Path traversal / LFI to AWS credential file
primitive: Directory traversal reads credential/config files on an EC2/container host (e.g. ~/.aws/credentials, task role env)
achieved_effect: AWS credential material read via path traversal, then used to reach S3/other services
notes: Pwned Labs 'Path Traversal to AWS credentials to S3'

name: Orphaned/dangling S3 bucket name takeover
primitive: Application/site references a deleted bucket name; attacker re-registers the globally-unique name
achieved_effect: Attacker-controlled bucket now serves content trusted by the victim app (reference/subdomain takeover)
notes: Pwned Labs 'Hijack Orphaned S3 Buckets for Data Access'

name: Publicly readable S3 bucket (ACL/policy grants AllUsers)
primitive: Bucket ACL or bucket policy grants s3:GetObject/ListBucket to AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers
notes: Classic static misconfig; Block Public Access off + public grant

name: Publicly writable S3 bucket (ACL/policy grants PutObject to AllUsers)
primitive: Bucket ACL/policy grants s3:PutObject to AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers
notes: Enables defacement/malware seeding and the writable-bucket-to-XSS chain

name: XXE file read / SSRF to AWS credentials
primitive: XML external entity injection reads local credential files (~/.aws/credentials) or performs SSRF to IMDS
achieved_effect: AWS credentials read from the host (local file or IMDS via XXE-driven SSRF)
notes: Pwned Labs 'File Upload XXE to Initial Access' (Lambda/SQLite)

name: Writable S3 bucket serving a site -> stored XSS -> admin session theft
primitive: Web-served S3 bucket is writable (public or leaked creds); attacker uploads content executed in victim browser context
achieved_effect: Admin session cookie/token captured via content injected into a writable, browser-served bucket
notes: Pwned Labs 'Leverage Writable S3 Bucket to Steal Admin Cookie' (Macie appears defensively)

name: SSM RCE on managed EC2 instances
primitive: ssm:SendCommand / ssm:StartSession / ssm:CreateAssociation against SSM-managed instances running the agent
achieved_effect: Arbitrary command execution (typically root/SYSTEM) on a managed EC2 instance, then instance-role credential theft
notes: HackTricks AWS SSM privesc; CreateAssociation persists without interactive session

name: Cross-account role assumption via leaked ExternalId
primitive: Third-party-integration role trusts an external account guarded only by an ExternalId that is leaked in an exposed config file
achieved_effect: Privileged cross-account role assumed by supplying the leaked ExternalId to sts:AssumeRole
notes: Pwned Labs 'Assume Privileged Role with External ID'; confused-deputy pattern

name: CloudTrail tampering to evade detection
primitive: cloudtrail:StopLogging / DeleteTrail / PutEventSelectors (or deleting the log bucket) blinds audit logging
achieved_effect: CloudTrail logging stopped/scoped-down so subsequent attacker actions are not recorded
notes: Defense-evasion; GuardDuty has a Stealth:IAMUser/CloudTrailLoggingDisabled finding

name: ECR image poisoning / supply-chain persistence
primitive: ecr:PutImage (or push over the task role) into a repo with mutable tags; poisoned image is pulled and run by ECS/EKS
achieved_effect: Attacker-controlled image pushed to ECR is pulled and executed by a production workload
notes: Posture precursor = mutable tags / no image-scan; Pwned Labs Inspector lab touches ECR scanning defensively

name: Event-driven IAM persistence backdoor
primitive: Attacker-created Lambda + EventBridge rule (or role trust to an external account) that re-mints access keys / re-attaches admin after cleanup
achieved_effect: Durable re-entry: credentials or admin policy automatically re-created after defenders revoke them
notes: AWSDoor-style; complements the create-access-key / update-assume-role-policy primitives

name: OS command injection on EC2 -> IMDS creds / user-data privesc
primitive: Command injection/RCE in an app on EC2; attacker queries IMDS or reads/rewrites user-data (ec2:ModifyInstanceAttribute) for boot-time code exec
achieved_effect: Code execution on the instance yields instance-role credentials from IMDS (and/or persisted user-data payload)
notes: Pwned Labs 'Command Injection to EC2 User Data Privilege Escalation'; also reads secrets baked into ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute userData

name: ECS task-role credential theft via task metadata endpoint
primitive: SSRF/RCE in a container reads $AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI at 169.254.170.2 to fetch the task role
achieved_effect: ECS task role credentials retrieved from the task metadata endpoint and usable against the AWS API
notes: On ECS-on-EC2, a container reaching 169.254.169.254 can also steal the more-privileged container-instance role (ECScape)

name: EKS pod-to-AWS credential theft (node role / IRSA)
primitive: Compromised pod without IMDS restriction steals the node instance role, or an over-broad IRSA service-account role via the projected web-identity token
achieved_effect: Node IAM role or IRSA role credentials obtained from inside a pod and used against AWS
notes: Pwned Labs 'Escalate from Prototype Pollution to EKS Takeover'; token at /var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token

name: IAM privesc: add self to a privileged group
primitive: iam:AddUserToGroup adds the attacker user to a group carrying admin policies
achieved_effect: Attacker user inherits the privileged group's permissions
notes: PACU method 13

name: IAM privesc: attach a managed admin policy to a controlled principal
primitive: iam:AttachUserPolicy / iam:AttachGroupPolicy / iam:AttachRolePolicy attaches AdministratorAccess
achieved_effect: AdministratorAccess (or equivalent) attached to an attacker-controlled user/group/role
notes: PACU methods 7-9

name: IAM privesc/persistence: mint access keys for a privileged user
primitive: iam:CreateAccessKey on another (higher-privileged) IAM user
achieved_effect: Working long-lived access key pair obtained for a more-privileged user
notes: PACU method 4; doubles as persistence (survives password/MFA controls)

name: IAM privesc: create a new default policy version
primitive: iam:CreatePolicyVersion on an attached customer-managed policy with --set-as-default granting Action:* Resource:*
achieved_effect: Attacker principal gains administrator permissions via a new default policy version
notes: PACU iam__privesc_scan method 1

name: IAM privesc: Lambda layer import-priority poisoning
primitive: lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration + lambda:AddLayerVersionPermission injects a layer that shadows boto3/deps in the import path
achieved_effect: Malicious layer executes inside the function and exfiltrates the execution-role credentials
notes: Rhino part 2 method; stealthy (code not visible in main function body)

name: IAM privesc: create/overwrite a console login profile
primitive: iam:CreateLoginProfile (set console password where none exists) or iam:UpdateLoginProfile (reset another user's password)
achieved_effect: Console access obtained as a targeted privileged user
notes: PACU methods 5-6

name: IAM privesc: PassRole to a CloudFormation stack
primitive: iam:PassRole + cloudformation:CreateStack deploys a template that acts with a privileged service role
achieved_effect: Stack created with a passed admin role provisions attacker-chosen privileged resources
notes: PACU method 20

name: IAM privesc: PassRole to AWS Data Pipeline
primitive: iam:PassRole + datapipeline:CreatePipeline + datapipeline:PutPipelineDefinition runs commands via the pipeline's EC2 resource role
achieved_effect: Command execution under the passed pipeline role, exposing its credentials
notes: PACU method 21 (legacy service, still present in older accounts)

name: IAM privesc: PassRole to a new EC2 instance
primitive: iam:PassRole + ec2:RunInstances launches an instance with a privileged instance profile; creds read from IMDS
achieved_effect: Privileged instance-profile credentials obtained from an EC2 instance the attacker launched
notes: PACU method 3; the canonical PassRole path

name: IAM privesc: PassRole to a Glue development endpoint
primitive: iam:PassRole + glue:CreateDevEndpoint (or glue:UpdateDevEndpoint on an existing one) gives SSH access running as the passed role
achieved_effect: Shell on a Glue dev endpoint yields the privileged role's credentials
notes: PACU methods 18-19

name: IAM privesc: PassRole to a new Lambda function
primitive: iam:PassRole + lambda:CreateFunction (+ lambda:InvokeFunction or lambda:CreateEventSourceMapping) runs attacker code under a privileged execution role
achieved_effect: Privileged Lambda execution-role credentials exfiltrated from attacker-supplied function code
notes: PACU methods 15-16 (direct invoke or DynamoDB/event trigger)

name: IAM privesc: SageMaker notebook role theft (with or without PassRole)
primitive: sagemaker:CreateNotebookInstance+CreatePresignedNotebookInstanceUrl+iam:PassRole (new notebook), OR sagemaker:ListNotebookInstances+CreatePresignedNotebookInstanceUrl (hijack an existing one, no PassRole)
achieved_effect: Terminal on a Jupyter notebook yields the attached SageMaker role's credentials
notes: Rhino part 2 methods 2-3

name: IAM privesc: add an inline admin policy
primitive: iam:PutUserPolicy / iam:PutGroupPolicy / iam:PutRolePolicy writes an inline policy granting *:*
achieved_effect: Inline allow-all policy embedded on an attacker-controlled principal
notes: PACU methods 10-12

name: IAM privesc: roll back to a prior permissive policy version
primitive: iam:SetDefaultPolicyVersion reverts a policy to an older, more-permissive stored version
achieved_effect: Principal regains elevated permissions by activating a previously-created permissive policy version
notes: Pwned Labs 'Escalate Privileges by IAM Policy Rollback'; PACU method 2

name: IAM privesc/persistence: backdoor a role's trust policy
primitive: iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy rewrites a privileged role's trust to allow the attacker principal, then sts:AssumeRole
achieved_effect: Attacker assumes a privileged role after injecting itself into that role's trust document
notes: PACU method 14; also a durable persistence primitive (external-account trust)

name: IAM privesc: overwrite existing Lambda code
primitive: lambda:UpdateFunctionCode replaces the code of a function that already has a privileged execution role
achieved_effect: Attacker code executes under the existing function's privileged role and leaks its credentials
notes: PACU method 17; no iam:PassRole required

name: KMS key policy grants broad/external decrypt
primitive: KMS key policy allows kms:Decrypt/kms:* to Principal:* or an untrusted account
notes: Undermines every secret/volume/snapshot encrypted under the key

name: Over-permissive S3 bucket policy grants cross-account/wildcard access
primitive: Bucket policy Principal:* or an untrusted account with broad s3:* and no condition guard
notes: Pwned Labs 'Exploit Weak Bucket Policies for Privileged Access'

name: SSRF to IMDS instance-role credential theft
primitive: SSRF-able app on an EC2 instance where IMDSv1 is reachable and an instance role is attached
achieved_effect: Instance role credentials actually retrieved from 169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials and usable against the AWS API
notes: Pwned Labs 'SSRF to Pwned'; impact = privileges of the instance role

name: Role trust policy allows Principal:* / arbitrary account
primitive: AssumeRole trust document allows Principal AWS:* or any account with no ExternalId/condition guard
notes: Static precursor to cross-account takeover; IAM Access Analyzer flags external-assumable roles

name: AWS account ID disclosure via public S3 bucket / access point ARN
primitive: Anonymously-readable S3 bucket or an s3:ResourceAccount/GetBucketPolicyStatus oracle that leaks the owning 12-digit account ID
achieved_effect: Target AWS account ID recovered from an unauthenticated position (seeds role-ARN enumeration)
notes: Pwned Labs 'Identify the AWS Account ID from a Public S3 Bucket'; bucket ownership/policy-condition side channel

name: Unauthenticated cross-account IAM principal enumeration
primitive: sts:AssumeRole / role-trust-policy update error differential reveals whether a principal ARN exists in another account (no creds needed)
achieved_effect: Valid IAM users/roles in the target account confirmed to exist without authenticating
notes: Pwned Labs 'Unauthenticated AWS IAM Principals Enumeration' (PACU); probing happens in attacker account, not logged in target CloudTrail

name: AMI / EBS / RDS snapshot shared publicly or with unknown accounts
primitive: CreateVolumePermission/ModifyImageAttribute/ModifyDBSnapshotAttribute set to 'all' or an untrusted account
notes: Static precursor to snapshot/AMI looting; scanners flag public share attributes

name: S3 bucket name brute-force discovery
primitive: Predictable/global S3 bucket namespace enumerated by wordlist against s3.amazonaws.com
achieved_effect: Existing bucket names discovered and their read/list access probed
notes: Pwned Labs 'S3 Bucket Brute Force to Breach', 'AWS S3 Enumeration Basics'

name: Stealth IAM permission enumeration via testIamPermissions
primitive: testIamPermissions returns only the caller's held permissions without producing admin-activity logs
achieved_effect: enumerated the caller identity's effective permissions on a project/resource by submitting a permission array to testIamPermissions and receiving the held subset
notes: *.testIamPermissions (e.g. resourcemanager.projects.testIamPermissions); basis of Pwned Labs IAM-fuzzing lab

name: BigQuery dataset exfiltration
primitive: bigquery.tables.getData + bigquery.jobs.create allow bulk read/export of datasets
achieved_effect: ran a query/extract job (jobs.insert) reading a table's rows or exported it to a bucket, obtaining the dataset contents
notes: bigquery.tables.getData + bigquery.jobs.create; export adds bigquery.tables.export + storage.objects.create

name: Cloud Storage object exfiltration
primitive: Broad storage.objects.get/list over sensitive buckets
achieved_effect: listed and downloaded sensitive objects (backups, keys, PII) from a bucket using storage.objects.list/get
notes: storage.objects.list / storage.objects.get; frequent state/backup/keyfile leakage

name: Secret Manager secret exfiltration
primitive: Over-broad secretmanager.versions.access on Secret Manager secrets
achieved_effect: accessed a secret version via secretmanager.versions.access and retrieved cleartext (DB creds / API keys) for further compromise
notes: secretmanager.versions.access (roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor); often over-granted at project scope

name: Serverless env-var secret harvest
primitive: Secrets embedded in Cloud Function / Cloud Run environment variables, readable via describe
achieved_effect: read a function/service configuration (functions.get / run.services.get) and extracted plaintext secrets from its environment variables
notes: cloudfunctions.functions.get / run.services.get exposes env vars; secrets should use Secret Manager refs

name: Exposed service-account key (repo / .git / commit)
primitive: SA key JSON committed to a public repo, exposed .git directory, or file leak
achieved_effect: authenticated with a leaked SA key JSON (gcloud auth activate-service-account) and confirmed access by calling an API as that SA
notes: private_key in key.json; Pwned Labs 'GitLab Commit' and exposed-.git labs

name: Metadata server SA token theft from a foothold
primitive: Attached instance/workload service account token readable from the link-local metadata endpoint after RCE/webshell/container access
achieved_effect: retrieved an OAuth access token for the attached SA from 169.254.169.254 and used it to authenticate a googleapis call (e.g. list a bucket / whoami)
notes: GET metadata/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token with Metadata-Flavor: Google; not SSRF-specific

name: SSRF to metadata server (gopher header injection)
primitive: Server-side request forgery reaching the metadata endpoint; gopher:// injects the required Metadata-Flavor header
achieved_effect: coerced the app to fetch the metadata token endpoint (adding Metadata-Flavor via gopher) and exfiltrated the SA access token
notes: gopher:// forges Metadata-Flavor: Google; Pwned Labs 'Exploit SSRF with Gopher' lab

name: GKE pod to node/cluster via metadata
primitive: Compromised pod reaches the node metadata server (Workload Identity/concealment off), stealing node SA token and kubelet bootstrap creds
achieved_effect: from a pod, pulled the node SA token (and/or kubelet TLS bootstrap creds via CSR) from the metadata endpoint and used it to read cluster secrets / reach cluster-admin
notes: node metadata computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts; kubelet TLS bootstrap CSR to cluster-admin

name: API key creation / harvest
primitive: serviceusage.apiKeys.create/list yields API keys that may bypass some restrictions
achieved_effect: created (or listed and reused) an API key and confirmed it authorized a restricted API call
notes: serviceusage.apiKeys.create / serviceusage.apiKeys.list

name: GCS HMAC key creation for persistence
primitive: storage.hmacKeys.create mints long-lived S3-style HMAC credentials for an SA
achieved_effect: created an HMAC key for an SA and used the access-id/secret to reach Cloud Storage via the XML/S3 API, surviving token rotation
notes: storage.hmacKeys.create; Pwned Labs 'create HMAC' labs; interop XML API creds

name: User-managed service-account keys present
primitive: Long-lived user-managed SA keys exist instead of short-lived credentials/Workload Identity
notes: keyType USER_MANAGED on SAs; enforce constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation

name: Cloud Build job SA abuse
primitive: cloudbuild.builds.create runs build steps as the Cloud Build SA (historically Editor)
achieved_effect: ran a build whose step read the Cloud Build SA's metadata token / performed a privileged action, yielding that SA's credentials
notes: cloudbuild.builds.create; @cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com; Pwned Labs 'Cloud Build for Privilege Escalation'

name: Cloud Function deploy with privileged runtime SA
primitive: cloudfunctions.functions.create + iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on a privileged runtime SA
achieved_effect: deployed a function bound to a more-privileged runtime SA and invoked it to steal that SA's metadata token
notes: cloudfunctions.functions.create + cloudfunctions.functions.setIamPolicy/actAs on runtime SA

name: Cloud Function code overwrite
primitive: cloudfunctions.functions.update lets an attacker inject code into an existing function
achieved_effect: overwrote an existing function's code and, on invocation, exfiltrated the function's runtime SA token
notes: cloudfunctions.functions.update; inherits the existing (often privileged) runtime SA

name: Cloud Run service deploy with privileged SA
primitive: run.services.create + iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on a privileged runtime SA
achieved_effect: deployed a Cloud Run service running as a more-privileged SA and pulled that SA's token from the container metadata endpoint
notes: run.services.create + actAs; container reads metadata token of the assigned SA

name: Cloud Scheduler job as privileged SA
primitive: cloudscheduler.jobs.create with an OAuth/OIDC target using a privileged SA
achieved_effect: created a scheduler job that invoked an attacker endpoint with a privileged SA's OAuth/OIDC token, capturing the token
notes: cloudscheduler.jobs.create + actAs on target SA; oauthToken/oidcToken added to the request

name: Compute instance create with privileged SA attached
primitive: compute.instances.create + iam.serviceAccounts.actAs to attach a privileged SA to a new VM
achieved_effect: launched a VM with a privileged SA attached and startup-script/SSH access, then read that SA's token from the VM metadata endpoint
notes: compute.instances.create + actAs (+ setMetadata/osLogin for shell); token from instance metadata

name: Add SSH key via instance setMetadata
primitive: compute.instances.setMetadata (or project-level) injects an authorized SSH key the guest agent honors
achieved_effect: added an ssh-keys metadata entry for a sudo user and logged into the VM, gaining a shell (and thus the instance SA token)
notes: compute.instances.setMetadata ssh-keys; guest agent auto-creates sudo user; Pwned Labs 'SET metadata' lab

name: Default service account with Editor attached to workloads
primitive: Compute/App Engine default SA retains roles/editor and is attached to VMs/functions
notes: PROJECTNUM-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com with Editor; any workload compromise inherits Editor

name: Deployment Manager runs as Google APIs SA
primitive: deploymentmanager.deployments.create executes as the Google APIs SA (Editor) without needing actAs
achieved_effect: submitted a Deployment Manager config that performed a privileged action (e.g. IAM binding / SA key) as the Editor-roled Google APIs SA
notes: deploymentmanager.deployments.create; runs as PROJECTNUM@cloudservices.gserviceaccount.com, actAs not required

name: GKE legacy metadata / Workload Identity disabled
primitive: Legacy metadata endpoints enabled or metadata concealment / Workload Identity not configured
notes: node config metadata.disable-legacy-endpoints / workloadMetadataConfig=GKE_METADATA; enable Workload Identity

name: Custom role permission injection
primitive: Principal can edit a custom role they are already granted (iam.roles.update)
achieved_effect: added a high-value permission to a custom role bound to the attacker and confirmed the new permission became usable
notes: iam.roles.update on an assigned custom role; silent expansion of own grants

name: Org policy constraint disable
primitive: orgpolicy.policy.set lets an attacker relax security constraints (e.g. disableServiceAccountKeyCreation)
achieved_effect: modified an org policy constraint (e.g. lifted SA-key-creation or public-IAM restriction) and confirmed the previously blocked action now succeeds
notes: orgpolicy.policy.set on constraints/iam.* ; enables downstream privesc/persistence

name: OS Login SSH via osAdminLogin + actAs
primitive: roles/compute.osAdminLogin plus iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the VM's SA grants sudo SSH
achieved_effect: SSH'd into an OS Login VM with sudo (osAdminLogin) and obtained a root shell plus the attached SA's metadata token
notes: compute.instances.osAdminLogin + actAs on instance SA (checked on every connect)

name: Project IAM policy self-grant
primitive: Principal can set the project IAM policy (resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy)
achieved_effect: added a binding granting the attacker identity roles/owner (or editor) on the project and confirmed the elevated role took effect
notes: resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy; folder/org setIamPolicy variants are equivalent higher up

name: OIDC identity token minting via getOpenIdToken
primitive: Principal can mint OIDC ID tokens for a target SA (iam.serviceAccounts.getOpenIdToken)
achieved_effect: minted an OIDC ID token for the target SA and used it to invoke an OIDC-gated resource (IAP-protected app, authenticated Cloud Run/Function)
notes: iam.serviceAccounts.getOpenIdToken; audience-scoped ID token for IAP/Run/Functions auth

name: Service account impersonation via getAccessToken
primitive: Principal holds Token Creator (iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken) over a more-privileged SA
achieved_effect: generated an OAuth access token for the target SA via iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken and used it to perform an action the caller could not (e.g. list a bucket / read a secret)
notes: iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken (roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator); gcloud --impersonate-service-account

name: Implicit delegation token chaining
primitive: Token Creator on an intermediary SA that itself holds Token Creator on a privileged SA (delegation chain)
achieved_effect: chained iam.serviceAccounts.implicitDelegation through an intermediary SA to generate an access token for the final privileged SA
notes: iam.serviceAccounts.implicitDelegation via delegates[] in generateAccessToken; Pwned Labs 'Implicit Delegation' lab

name: Service-account user-managed key creation
primitive: Principal can create long-lived keys for a target SA (iam.serviceAccountKeys.create)
achieved_effect: created a new user-managed key for the target SA and authenticated with it to act as that SA (also a persistence primitive)
notes: iam.serviceAccountKeys.create (roles/iam.serviceAccountKeyAdmin); non-expiring credential

name: Service-account IAM policy self-grant
